From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 11:12:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: Redwood <> FinTechCo procurement & marketplace options

Hi Samira / Ben —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Call highlights
- FinTechCo is evaluating Redwood for customer-facing transaction analytics (sensitive PII redaction in-pipeline).
- Primary procurement path today is AP/PO for vendor SaaS, but the team is interested in whether AWS Marketplace would speed approval for a pilot.
- Commercial ask: sample invoice and clarity on PO-via-marketplace vs direct invoicing, and any startup/PO discounts.
- Security: SOC2 report and network isolation questions — Marissa will follow with specifics.

Proposed next steps
1) I attached our latest pricing sheet (redwood_pricing_sheet_v3.pdf). Please confirm which SKU you want priced for a 6-month pilot.
2) Samira/Ben: can you confirm whether procurement will accept an AWS Marketplace subscription (i.e., vendor-managed billing through AWS) or if you need direct PO to Redwood? If both are possible, what is the preferred path for pilot?
3) I'll drop our Marketplace onboarding checklist and the SOC2 link to help procurement evaluate marketplace onboarding time.
4) We’ll prepare a short commercial summary and a sample invoice if you prefer PO.

If we get confirmation on preferred procurement path by EOD Mon (2/23) we can target a 2-week vendor setup for pilot access.

Thanks —

Dev Patel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0124
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Recap: Redwood <> FinTechCo procurement & marketplace options

Hi Dev —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few quick answers from our side: 

- Procurement preference: default is AP/PO (we run vendor onboarding through our AP system). We are exploring AWS Marketplace as a secondary route because it sometimes bypasses the vendor onboarding paperwork for smaller pilots and gets budget owners to approve faster.
- For the pilot (6 weeks), my recommendation is: start with AWS Marketplace if you can support it (we can spin up a subscription quickly), but keep direct PO as the fallback if marketplace billing is not practical for the pilot.
- Action items for us: I attached our PO template (FinTechCo_PO_Template.pdf) so you can validate the required fields (PO number, remit address, tax info). Ben (cc'd) will lead the vendor setup.

Ben — can you confirm the typical lead time for vendor setup assuming we pursue the PO route? Also, would you need an executed MSA or is a PO with standard T&Cs sufficient for a pilot under $50k?

Appreciate the SOC2 and marketplace checklist — please send the docs and any marketplace onboarding steps.

Best,
Samira Khan
Senior Product Manager, Data Platform | FinTechCo
samira.k@fintechco.com | +1 (212) 555-1410
Attachment(s): FinTechCo_PO_Template.pdf (pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@fintechco.com>, Ben Liu <ben.liu@fintechco.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Feb 2026 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: Redwood <> FinTechCo procurement & marketplace options

Thanks Samira — cc'ing procurement and looping in a couple quick notes from our side that might help accelerate the marketplace path: 

- Marketplace pros: faster provisioning, consolidated billing through AWS, often quicker approvals for pilot dollar amounts.
- Marketplace cons: some enterprises require additional procurement paperwork to map billing centers; marketplace SKUs sometimes limit contract customizations.
- We can offer a short-term pilot SKU on AWS Marketplace that mirrors our direct-plan pricing and include a one-time onboarding credit if you select Marketplace for the pilot.

Attached is our Marketplace onboarding checklist (Marketplace_Onboarding_Checklist.docx) and a link to our SOC2 report. If Ben can share the billing remit address and the PO field requirements (PO number, invoice recipient email, tax id), we’ll generate a sample invoice and a minimal MSA for signature.

Quick ask: Ben — what is your typical vendor setup SLA? If it's >2 weeks on PO route that pushes us to recommend Marketplace for speed.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0177
Attachment(s): Marketplace_Onboarding_Checklist.docx (docx)

Dev / Samira —

Appreciate the summaries. A few procurement-specific items from my side: 

1) Vendor setup SLA: typically 10 business days from receipt of a completed vendor packet + MSA. If you can provide a sample invoice and a redacted MSA, we can queue Redwood. For pilots under $50k our legal bar is lower but we do need the vendor in Ariba and a tax W-9 on file.

2) PO vs Marketplace: we can do either. Marketplace is preferred by the business team for speed, but our AP team still needs a record in Ariba for reconciliation when charges hit the AWS bill. If you support AWS Marketplace SCA (subscription consolidated billing) that's ideal. Otherwise, we'll use direct PO and route payments via our AP process.

3) Invoice requirements: billing remit address — FinTechCo, Inc., AP Dept, 101 Market St, Suite 400, San Francisco, CA 94105. Invoices need the PO number on the first page and an email copy to ap-invoices@fintechco.com.

4) Timeline: if we get the vendor packet + sample invoice by EOD Wed (2/25), we can provision in 8–10 business days. Otherwise marketplace subscription may be the faster path for a pilot starting in early March.

Please send the sample invoice and MSA link. If it's easier, we can accept DocuSign for the MSA.

Thanks,
Ben Liu
Procurement Manager | FinTechCo
ben.liu@fintechco.com | +1 (415) 555-0900
